answers.note: I like presenting the option to close so we never accidentally close what should continue to be an open event. That's a far bigger problem.

I think we can do a better job making this feel like a reward moment when we confidently know each event has ended. Where I want to be careful is ever wrongly assuming an event has ended, as well as flipping an event into a more "ended" feeling, rather than allowing it to operate as normal after the event date if needed. I think the win here would be more a singular moment of presentation, where's on the next either login or event page click in (not sure best UX here), we kind of announce an 'everything is ready!' type of delight, so once they continue past that they're still able to upload/interact as they're used to, not shifting the experience on them, especially for first time hosts who may not expect a major shift from pre-to-post-event.

Again, we need to be very careful about how we're flipping event UI after an event ends. I think it will be incredibly common for guests to come back to the event the next day and upload their media, rather than only expecting them to upload the day of. That's a big reason why I wanted the host to have the option to close the event directly (from an earlier question this batch) rather than us ever handling it automatically ourselves. Or let's say I create an event for a trip with friends and I simply put in a single date on there, but wanted to stay open for the entire week. I was too lazy to add a date range, but expect it to keep working over the course of the week for everyone.

I'm conflicted here. On one hand, using the cover photograph or a strip of its photographs feels much more social and alive, encouraging the click into the event. Also, more custom than a generic card for every event guests get sent on partyreel. However, I'm worried that for many events where user-uploaded media isn't as cool as what we're able to use in marketing, these cards would present as more sloppy than beautiful. For that reason, our own card design provides more polished consistency. We could also provide some variation with seeds or something, such as our thinking about colors for the event head in another question from this batch Additionally, for more private events, we would need a fallback design anyway since private images shouldn't be included in the social link passed around. Excited to see what you come up with next.

I love how easy this makes it for guests to go straight into becoming a host rather than dropping them off in marketing and trying to convince them into it. Additionally, I like having that extra reminder at the end of an album, but I think we can make it more polished and subtle so it doesn't feel like marketing to hosts. Could even be beneath guests so it doesn't get too in the way of real content.
